body.estimand_functional: \(D_k(n)=\max_{(G,T,e)\in\mathcal G_{n,k},\ d_e(G)<\infty}[K_G(\lambda_e):K_G]\). For \(n\geq4\), the proved two-sided envelope is \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\), with \(D_k(6)\leq\min\{2^{k+1},24\}\). Exact equality \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) holds when \(n\geq2k+4\), and the exact table is \(D_0(2)=1\), \(D_k(3)=1\), \(D_k(4)=2\), \(D_0(5)=2\), \(D_1(5)=3\), and \(D_k(5)=4\) for \(k\geq2\). At zero excess the dispatcher returns the exact published \(1/2/\infty\) tree classification and finite \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions; at positive excess its unconditional algebraic branch retains the explicit computable report \(d_e(G)\leq2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}\) and does not claim to compute \(\tau_{n-1}\). A rational-circuit representation of \(p_e(t)\) is delivered only under the valid-chart and successful-output conditions of \(\mathrm{thm:conditional\mbox{-}geometric\mbox{-}resolution}\).

sampling_model.design: The identification layer uses the exact population covariance of a known recursive Gaussian mixed graph. The unconditional symbolic layer returns an algebraic-versus-transcendental queried-coordinate tag. The estimation layer is available at fixed \(G,n\) only after a valid source-prime chart has produced a successful finite eliminant and certificate.
sampling_model.treatment: There is no designated treatment; the causal query is the direct structural coefficient \(\lambda_e\).
sampling_model.nuisance_estimation: Conditional on \(d_e(G)<\infty\), a valid source-prime chart, and successful geometric-resolution output, project \(S_m\) smoothly onto the regular covariance-model stratum, evaluate the returned certificate circuits and \(p_e\), isolate every simple real root, and retain roots by exact local real-extension status. On the unconditional transcendental tag the finite-set rung does not apply; on an algebraic tag without a valid chart, no unavailable polynomial or branch estimator is imputed.

comparator_promise_table.comparator_claim: TreeID introduced the missing-bidirected-cycle method for the same zero-excess tree-shaped class; the 2022 paper did not itself prove completeness.

Theorem 27 and Sections 1.1--2.1 give the complete per-parameter \(1/2/\infty\) algorithm and finite expressions on the tree-shaped class, which is exactly \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\) after the harmless vertex-count indexing shift and is not \(\mathcal G_{n,k}\) for positive \(k\).
Theorem 1 accelerates the complete tree-only predicate implemented by fasttreeid; it does not supply the positive-excess exact degree or eliminant.
Example 8, Figure 5(b), and Section 7 supply the published five-vertex whole-fiber cubic used here to derive the coordinate lower bound \(D_1(5)\geq3\); the cubic graph itself is not a novelty claim.
Theorem 3.3 and Corollary 3.4 transfer rational identification from ancestral induced subgraphs, not higher finite coordinate degree.
Corollary 6 places generic edge identifiability in polynomial space without returning a positive-excess algebraic-coordinate degree or eliminant.
Theorems 4.4 and 5.1 concern minimum bounded-degree rational formulas, a different degree notion from single-coordinate algebraic extension degree.
The solver computes geometric resolutions under a reduced regular-sequence hypothesis away from a supplied inequation and does not construct the source-prime chart required here.
Theorem 1 handles arbitrary equations and an inequation with complexity depending on intermediate geometric degree, but does not select the embedded SEM source prime.
Theorem 2.1 constructs a generic rational univariate representation after a suitable generically zero-dimensional parametric presentation is available.
The paper computes separating forms and rational univariate representations for bivariate systems after their polynomial presentation is supplied.
The paper derives inference for criterion-defined identified sets; the present finite-branch result is proved only on a supplied-valid-chart and successful-output regular domain.
The preprint derives regular inference for rational half-trek estimators; the present singleton conclusion is conditional on successful chart-certified finite output.
The paper distinguishes global real identifiability from generic algebraic behavior; the present real-root result likewise retains a root only after a real supported lift.

body.tldr: Adding parents to a supplied rooted tree creates finite ambiguity measured here by the single-coordinate complex degree \(D_k(n)\), not by whole-fiber cardinality or real root count. For \(n\geq4\), the paper proves \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\), where \(\tau_b\) is the largest prescribed-indegree fiber of labeled tournaments on \(b\) vertices; the recurrence certificate gives \(\tau_5=24\) and hence \(D_k(6)\leq\min\{2^{k+1},24\}\). It also proves \(D_k(n)=2^{k+1}\) for \(n\geq2k+4\) and the exact frontier for every \(n\leq5\). The tournament ceiling is not claimed attained in the only unresolved region, \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\). Because \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\) is exactly the published tree class, the unconditional dispatcher retains its complete \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite expressions at zero excess; positive excess currently receives an exact algebraic-versus-transcendental Jacobian tag and the existing efficiently reportable size-binomial ceiling. Exact positive-excess polynomials, exceptional sets, real lifting, and regular inference are proved on the supplied-valid-chart and successful-output domain of the conditional geometric-resolution theorem.

project_justification.gap: The published tree algorithms completely solve exactly \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\), not \(\mathcal G_{n,k}\) for positive \(k\). General mixed-graph work studies rational recovery, whole-parameter fibers, or unparameterized elimination, and does not give the maximum finite degree of one original directed coefficient as a function of both vertex size and excess-parent budget. General geometric-resolution algorithms also do not select the embedded SEM source prime or provide bounded descent over the implicitly presented covariance field.
project_justification.niche: Distance from a supplied arborescence creates a parameterized algebraic regime in which the orientation system yields a projection-aware ceiling and explicit constructions yield sharp size-sensitive lower bounds. The zero-excess class inherits a complete published algorithm, while positive excess separates the unconditional algebraicity tag from chart-certified exact finite output.
project_justification.fill: The paper proves the projection-aware tournament score-fiber upper bound and the two-sided envelope \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\leq D_k(n)\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\) for \(n\geq4\), including \(\tau_5=24\) and the six-vertex cap, the large-size equality, the inherited all-size lower envelope, and the exact \(n\leq5\) coordinate-degree frontier. It isolates the remaining positive-\(k\), \(n\geq6\) small-size frontier in \(\mathrm{oeq:sharp\mbox{-}size\mbox{-}frontier}\) without claiming that the tournament cap is attained there. It supplies an unconditional randomized Jacobian-rank tag, retains the complete published tree-case output at \(k=0\), and proves a conditional geometric-resolution theorem with explicit straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence. Exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results hold only on the supplied-valid-chart and successful-output domain.

body.related_work: Van der Zander, Wienöbst, Bläser, and Liśkiewicz introduced TreeID for directed-tree linear SEMs. On this same zero-excess class, Gupta and Bläser proved that each queried coefficient has generically one, two, or infinitely many values and returned the finite values as FASTPs; Briefs and Bläser accelerated that tree-only algorithm in fasttreeid. This cited zero-excess theorem is consumed only by \(\mathrm{lem:tree\mbox{-}class\mbox{-}algorithm\mbox{-}transfer}\); it does not extend to positive \(k\). Equivalently, the published tree class is exactly \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\), up to the harmless vertex-count indexing shift, and is not \(\mathcal G_{n,k}\) for positive \(k\). Foygel, Draisma, and Drton give the published five-node whole-fiber cubic used here only as the \(D_1(5)\) coordinate base case; their cubic and other small higher-degree examples are not novelty claims. Hollering, Misra, and Sturma optimize bounded-degree rational formulas, a different degree notion. Giusti, Lecerf, and Salvy compute geometric resolutions for reduced regular sequences away from an inequation (DOI 10.1006/jcom.2000.0571), and Lecerf treats arbitrary equations and inequations with complexity charged to intermediate geometric degree (DOI 10.1016/S0885-064X(03)00031-1); neither selects the embedded source component or manufactures its source-nonzero chart. The exceptional-set, real-lifting, regular-cell, root-separation, finite-set, and singleton-inference results are proved only after a valid chart and successful conditional output are supplied; they cover every retained branch without claiming discriminant-uniform inference or automatic branch selection.
body.technical_internal_limitation: For \(k>0\), \(n\geq6\), and \(n<2k+4\), the exact frontier remains between \(2^{\min\{k+1,\lfloor(n-2)/2\rfloor\}}\) and \(\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\): the complete-tournament score fiber is only a combinatorial ceiling, and SEM branches may be lost through forced covariance relations, exact localization, affine dehomogenization, or projective infinity. The bound gives \(D_k(6)\leq\min\{2^{k+1},24\}\), but no attaining six-vertex SEM family is asserted. The unconditional fixed-parameter dispatcher retains the efficiently explicit size-binomial cap because this round supplies no uniform exact \(\tau_{n-1}\) computation and certificate for arbitrary \(n\) within its runtime. The exhaustive five-node orbit census remains a secondary regression and coordinate-census question because the cubic and quartic base cases and the entire \(n\leq5\) frontier are fixed. Independently, the quadratic core does not construct a reduced local presentation of the embedded source prime or bounded rational-circuit descent over \(K_G\). On the certified event determined by a supplied valid source-prime chart, the exceptional-set theorem, real-root-lifting theorem, regular-cell lemma, derived root-separation lemma, regular finite-set inference theorem, and singleton inference proposition hold. Their chart antecedent appears in every statement; no chart-free statistical theorem is asserted. Coordinate localization is never promoted to equality of full fibers, real roots are never equated with real supported lifts, and local rank is not used to assert real uniqueness.
body.honest_scope: The paper proves the full frontier through five vertices, the all-size lower envelope, the tournament score-fiber ceiling \(D_k(n)\leq\min\{2^{k+1},\tau_{n-1}\}\), the explicit consequence \(D_k(6)\leq\min\{2^{k+1},24\}\), and the large-size equality, but not the remaining positive-excess small-size strip; the tournament cap is not claimed attained there. In the equality regime, comparison with the existing one-sink witness entails \(\tau_{n-1}\geq2^{k+1}\), so the sharper ceiling preserves that result. Unconditionally, the dispatcher returns the complete published \(1/2/\infty\) classification and finite \(\operatorname{FASTP}\) expressions on \(\mathcal G_{n,0}\). For \(|D\setminus T|>0\), it returns only a randomized algebraic-versus-transcendental tag, a rank or dominance certificate, and the efficiently available ceiling \(d_e(G)\leq2^{\min\{|D|-n+2,\binom{n-2}{2}\}}\); it does not compute \(\tau_{n-1}\), \(d_e(G)\), \(p_e\), \(\mathcal Q_{G,e}\), or \(h_{G,e}\) on the algebraic branch. Given valid source-prime charts and successful output, the conditional geometric-resolution theorem returns the exact finite objects with its stated straight-line-program and intermediate-degree dependence. On precisely that same conditional domain, the six exceptional-set, real-lifting, and regular-inference results are proved. No discriminant-uniform inference, automatic branch selection, or all-singular-covariance guarantee is claimed, and positive definiteness of recovered noise follows only after a complete real supported lift by congruence.
